title: Troubleshooting Decision Trees
contentStatus: PROPOSED title/content, pending DiFacto confirmation. Grounded in SOW Bucket 2 'troubleshooting curriculum: decision trees and troubleshooting procedures for L3A technicians.' Specific decision tree content pending DiFacto engineering documentation.

sections.title: From Methodology to Structured Tools
learningObjectives: Understand how this module builds on the root cause methodology from Module 5
Recognize the purpose of a decision tree as a diagnostic aid
sections.content: L3A-M5 established the general methodology for root cause diagnosis. This module formalizes that into decision trees - structured, repeatable diagnostic paths for common fault categories. A decision tree doesn't replace judgment, but it ensures a consistent, efficient diagnostic sequence rather than reinventing the approach each time a similar issue appears.

keyTerms.note: A structured diagnostic sequence of yes/no or condition-based questions leading systematically toward identifying a root cause.

sections.title: How a Decision Tree Is Structured
learningObjectives: Understand the general format of a troubleshooting decision tree
Recognize how branching works within the structure
sections.content: A decision tree starts with a broad symptom category and branches based on answers to diagnostic questions, narrowing toward a specific likely cause at each step. The key discipline is answering each branch point honestly based on what's actually observed, rather than skipping ahead to a cause that seems likely without confirming the branch conditions.

sections.title: Navigation-Related Decision Trees
learningObjectives: Understand the general branch logic for navigation-related symptoms
Recognize how this connects to sensor and mapping knowledge from earlier training
sections.content: Navigation-related troubleshooting typically branches on questions like: is the issue isolated to one area of the map or does it occur everywhere, has anything physically changed in that area, does the issue correlate with specific lighting or surface conditions. Specific decision tree content for MoRo's navigation troubleshooting is being developed with DiFacto's engineering team.

sections.title: Mechanical and Power Decision Trees
learningObjectives: Understand the general branch logic for mechanical and power-related symptoms
Recognize how this connects to maintenance knowledge from earlier modules
sections.content: Mechanical and power troubleshooting branches on different questions: is the symptom constant or intermittent, does it correlate with battery charge level, has recent maintenance or a recent incident preceded the symptom's appearance. These decision trees draw directly on the preventive and predictive maintenance knowledge built in Modules 2-4.

sections.title: When a Decision Tree Doesn't Resolve the Issue
learningObjectives: Understand what to do when following a decision tree doesn't lead to a clear cause
Recognize this as a signal for escalation, not a failure of the technician
sections.content: Decision trees cover common, well-understood fault patterns - they won't cover every possible issue. If following a tree to its end doesn't produce a confident root cause, that's the signal to escalate per the criteria covered in L3A-M5, rather than guessing beyond what the structured process supports.

sections.title: Contributing to Decision Tree Improvement
learningObjectives: Understand how field experience feeds back into improving decision trees over time
Recognize the technician's role in this improvement process
sections.content: Decision trees aren't static - as technicians encounter new fault patterns in the field, that experience can inform updates to the decision trees used across the fleet. Documenting unusual diagnoses thoroughly, the same habit covered in Module 1, is what makes this feedback loop possible.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a troubleshooting decision tree?
options: To provide a structured, repeatable diagnostic path for common fault categories
questions.feedback: Correct. Decision trees structure diagnosis without replacing the judgment that guides them.

questions.question: What's the key discipline when working through a decision tree?
options: Skip ahead to the most likely cause immediately
Answer each branch point honestly based on what's actually observed
Always start from the most complex branch
questions.feedback: Correct. Honest, observed answers at each branch point are what make the tree reliable.

questions.question: What kind of question typically starts a navigation-related decision tree branch?
options: Whether the issue is isolated to one map area or occurs everywhere
The time of day the robot was purchased
questions.feedback: Correct. Isolating whether an issue is localized or widespread is a typical early branch point.

questions.question: What should happen if following a decision tree doesn't produce a confident root cause?
options: Keep guessing randomly until something works
Escalate, per the criteria covered in root cause methodology
Ignore the issue since the tree didn't resolve it
questions.feedback: Correct. An inconclusive decision tree result is a signal to escalate, not a technician failure.

questions.question: How do decision trees improve over time?
options: Field experience and thorough documentation feed back into updating them
Only DiFacto engineering updates them, with no field input
questions.feedback: Correct. Technician field experience, well-documented, feeds the improvement of decision trees.
